neighbours.label: a phrase marking an appearance that later turns out otherwise (at first glance, or so I thought, to untrained eyes, on the surface)
fire: At first sight, the contract looks like a good deal for tenants.
The plan seemed simple enough on paper, but it collapsed within weeks.
To the casual observer, the old mill appears to be abandoned.
Everything was going well, or so she believed, until the letter came.
On the surface, the two brothers could hardly be more alike.
At first glance, the numbers suggest that crime is falling.
To an untrained eye, the forged signature would seem perfectly genuine.
We had finally beaten the flood, or so we thought.
quiet: At the meeting, the contract was signed by a group of tenants.
The plan was printed on paper, and it was mailed within weeks.
To the north of town, the old mill stands next to the river.
Everything was packed in boxes, and she carried them until the car came.
On the farm, the two brothers worked side by side every day.
At the end, the numbers were added and sent to the office.
To an old friend, he sent a signed copy of his new book.
We had finally reached the river, and we made camp.

notes: Card: ' glance' x3, ' thought' x3, ' surface' x2, ' eyes', plus ',' and '.' that end such setups. A distinction, not a list. Probes: 'on the surface' 0.496, 'or so I thought' 0.487, 'at first glance' 0.456, 'to untrained eyes' 0.426; plain versions under 0.03. The test uses new variants too (at first sight, on paper, to the casual observer), and near misses keep the frames.
